title: Ongoing mulch management on a no-dig bed
subtitle: How to maintain soil cover and fertility year after year without digging.
excerpt: A no-dig bed requires a regular top-dressing of compost to maintain fertility and keep the soil protected. This is the annual maintenance routine: timing, quantities, and what to do with the compost surface after each crop is cleared.
sourceNotes: No-dig maintenance method from Charles Dowding, No Dig Organic Home and Garden (2013) and Organic Gardening (2010). Compost application rates from Garden Organic guidance.

glossaryTerms.definition: Applying compost, well-rotted manure, or other organic matter to the surface of a bed without digging it in. Worms and soil organisms incorporate it over time. Top-dressing maintains soil structure and fertility on a no-dig bed without the disruption of cultivation.

content.text: A no-dig bed works by protecting the soil surface and adding organic matter from above. The bed needs a
of well-made compost at least once a year, and ideally twice. This replaces what crops have taken out and keeps weed pressure low.

Apply 2 to 5 cm of well-rotted compost as a top-dressing in autumn after crops are cleared. Spread evenly across the entire bed surface. Do not dig it in: leave it on the surface and plant or sow directly into it in spring. In the first year of converting a lawn or rough ground, apply 15 cm to suppress weeds.

When a crop finishes, cut the stem at ground level rather than pulling up the roots. The root system decomposing in the soil adds organic matter and leaves channels for water. Clear weeds before they set seed, by hand or with a hoe running just below the surface.
In summer gaps between crops, sow a quick cover crop (phacelia or buckwheat) rather than leaving the surface bare. This suppresses annual weeds and keeps the soil active.
Signs the bed needs more compost

If the soil surface is compacted and bare after rain, or if crops are growing poorly despite correct spacing and watering, the organic matter level has dropped. Top-dress immediately with 5 cm of compost and reassess after the next crop.
